SereneLife Battery Grass Cutter, Grass Clippers Cordless, Trimmer Cutter, Handheld Trimmer, Grass Shear Electric, Perfect for Leaves & Debris, Rechargeable Battery, Charge Time 4 Hrs, 3.6V Here are my thoughts about Roku. Generally I like the product, but in setting it up I had some concerns.

PROS:
**Easy to set up
**Compact - it's so small it fits in one hand.
**Picture quality is pretty sharp depending upon the source. It is not HD quality but more like a decent DVD (though not Blu-Ray).
**A number of free channels available through Roku. You can add a lot of content. Since I'm an old movie buff, I added Pub a Hub (public domain movies) and Crackle (pretty bad recent movies but some good classics, like Easy Rider).
**Picture is big. I have a friend who has a projector that's five times as big as the Roku, and yet the projected image is the same size. That's impressive.

CONS:
**How much radiation does this device emit? In the fine print, the instruction booklet reads: "This equipment complies with FCC radiation exposure limits set forth for an uncontrolled environment. This equipment should be installed and operated with minimum distance 20CM between the RADIATOR AND YOUR BODY."
Hmm. I don't know about you, but it's hard not to sit pretty close to the projector. I used it in the bedroom and watched a movie on the ceiling. Of course I had to be close to it in order to put it at the right angle. How much radiation is the device emitting?

**Roku asks for your credit card information before you can use the device. When you set up an account, even if you don't want anything other than the free channels, they force you to put your credit card on file. The other privacy issue I object to is the way Roku allows you to connect to Facebook. In order for Roku to work, you were pretty much forced to allow Roku to access your information on Facebook at any time (even when you're logged out!) Not happy about this.

**In order to add some channels to the Roku network, you have to establish separate accounts. That means establishing one for Netflix, one for Amazon, etc, if you don't already have one. This means I'm sharing my account information with a number of companies I may or may not want to do business with. No doubt all this information will be shared among the video providers. That means a lot of spam will be coming my way in my email.

**Roku is geared toward convincing you to subscribe to as many streaming (pay on demand) services as possible. I'm not sure I would pay $300 for it, as it is very much a device aimed to getting you to subscribe to streaming channels. You can use it other ways, but Roku feels like a product sponsored by many vendors, as opposed to a stand-alone projector.

My conclusion? I recommend it with some reservations as noted above.
text_fidelity_b: SereneLife Battery Grass Cutter, Grass Clippers Cordless, Trimmer Cutter, Handheld Trimmer, Grass Shear Electric, Perfect for Leaves & Debris, Rechargeable Battery, Charge Time 4 Hrs, 3.6V

Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 This will be a fairly detailed and honest review.

1. Who is this for?
This computer is what I would consider a gateway computer. Those who are looking at upgrading a fairly old or not so powerful laptop and are looking to do a little more productivity, this is a great option.

2. What do you get?
Well you can probably read the description, however it's worth noting. You get an Intel i7 7500u CPU (dual core with 4 threads) 12gb DDR4 RAM, Nvidia 940mx GPU, a 256gb SSD, 15.6" 1080p screen, fingerprint reader, and a backlit keyboard.

The reason I mention all of the feautures is because you would be hardpressed to find another laptop with these features for the same price. To my knowledge there is not laptop on the market for $800 with an i7, dedicated graphics, 12gb of RAM and an SSD. This is really one of the best values on the market right now.

With all of that said, this isn't for everyone. If you want to do extensive gaming, this is not for you. Can it game? Yes, light gaming can be achieved, however it isn't marketed as a gaming laptop. Is this for someone who wants to do editing (video, audio, photos)? Yes, again light editing can be achieved.

What blew me away with this computer is the speakers! They are fantastic! I usually use headphones and would consider myself somewhat picky with sound, and for laptop speakers these are really something great.

This computer is really a middle of the pack all arounders dream. If you dabble in a little of this and a little of that but don't do anything professionally or extremely serious, this is really all you need.

Also, everyone's experience is different. Some hate loud fans, and if this is pushed the fans will be audible. Some don't like that the backlit keyboard times out after 30 seconds of no use. These things really don't bother me.

Lastly, the versatility of this laptop is really great. I've bought tablets and sold them because I couldn't justify having a laptop and tablet, then bought tablets again because I missed the things I could do with them that I was missing on a laptop. This solved all of those issues except size. It's pretty big, which for some is a plus others its not.

Overall, if you are looking at upgrading and don't want to spend $1,200-2,000 on a flagship model laptop this is a great option! I can't recommend this enough.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229

Technics Premium in- Ear Monitors IEM, High-Fidelity Wired in-Ear Earbuds Earphones with Innovative 10mm Driver for Ultra-Low Distortion - EAH-TZ700, Black/Gold I work in live AV production, and usually keep a pair of Sony over-the-ear headphones in my gear bag for monitoring sound on location. Quality of the sound is important for concert and other live music gigs. But those big Sonys take up a lot of space, so I've been considering a good set of IEMs for a while now. In the past I haven't had good results from anything that wasn't a large over-the-ear set, and I have small ears that reject a lot of ear-bud style devices so I was excited to get a chance to try these out.

Ok, to be fair, I don't have any other IEMs to compare this to, but I'm BLOWN AWAY at how incredible they sound at such a miniscule size. I put on the smallest tips for my ears and they actually stay in relatively well, and create the passive noise cancellation I was expecting but without being uncomfortable to wear for an extended period of time. But the range of sound reproduced was something I have only experienced in larger studio headphones!
A perk of IEMs versus larger headphones on jobs like mine are that I can pull out one so I can hear the sound around me while monitoring with my other ear (great if working with an audio engineer who needs to communicate with me on the job), and it comes with a pretty nifty case to wrap it up and slide into my bag. The case makes it bigger than it needs to be, but honestly this is so much less space than my old headphones took up, and keeps the cord from getting tangled. I love it!
For personal use, they sound great even on consumer equipment, but they really shine on devices that can drive the additional range such as my old LG V20 with it's Quad DAC built in (one of the reasons I keep that old device around!).
The price tag is a little steep for me personally, but my Sony headphones retail somewhere around this (I had bought them used), and I KNOW there are pricier options out there, so it seems to fit right into the audiophile equipment range.
text_fidelity_b: Technics Premium in- Ear Monitors IEM, High-Fidelity Wired in-Ear Earbuds Earphones with Innovative 10mm Driver for Ultra-Low Distortion - EAH-TZ700, Black/Gold

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Whole Home Bundle | Video Doorbell System, Outdoor camera, and Mini camera | HD video, motion detection, Works with Alexa I’m 50/50 on the Blink XT2. It’s a decent system that has non contractual usage, which is very awesome... I just find a couple of issues with the system performance. There are no options for notification updates or changes to the system and the only tone that it will play doesn’t not work all me up at night. Also, you can arm the system on a schedule, which is cool, but again system options are limited. I have cameras that surround my house but, my dogs are always setting off the backyard cams... which happens all day and night. You can’t just arm the front yard cameras for all day use while turning off the rear cameras so the dogs don’t set them off in the day time. This means if you’re armed and home, your phone will go off alllllllllll day, and basically be ineffective for monitoring. We have a pool so all day long I’m also going in and out the house and it just adds to the notifications. I hoped this unit would allow more function in settings but it’s just very basic. There are a couple neat Alexa add one, but I refuse to buy Alexa for several reasons and feel there is a ploy to have to buy Alexa when those features like voice announcements or lights turning on upon motion. I like the system for its purpose, but the function and personalization falls flat on its face and that’s the reason it’s not 5 stars. I’ve read posts and there is AMPLE feedback to Blink/Amazon to correct the notifications (again notification ringer is ineffective unless awake and CANNOT BE CHANGED) but isn’t fixed. I have iphone, heard android users have a little more function??? Yet another uncorrected design flaw.

Also, the system crashes from WiFi for no identified reason and requires you to mess with the system. Doesn’t take long but had this a week and happened twice while I’m out and renders the system useless.

Another issue is that there is a 10-15 second delay to speak live through the cameras, even with early detection on. Still helpful, but trying to talk to someone through the cameras, like a delivery guy or unexpected guest, creates a lot of awkward conversations through the system.

Ideally... it works, and will help, but personalization and lack of settings to help your needs of the system can find a lot of improvement and hope these system flaws are improved as they are completely within the ability to improve function of their designs. Had these issues not been present the system would get 5 stars as the cameras are great, the system is very easy to install and get going, adds piece of mind that you otherwise wouldn’t have with out a high dollar monthly contract. All in all, it’s an improvement to safety, but many things can improve to make it effective and useful. Until then, it’s just bland
text_fidelity_b: Blink Whole Home Bundle | Video Doorbell System, Outdoor camera, and Mini camera | HD video, motion detection, Works with Alexa

TBMax Cat 8 Ethernet Cable 25 ft, High Speed Cat8 40Gbps 2000MHz LAN Cord with Gold Plated RJ45 Connectors, S/FTP Shielded Network Patch Cable for Gaming/Xbox/Modem/Router -White I have used and tested more Ethernet cables than I can remember and there is no question, all Ethernet cables are not created equally.

Typically any device requiring an Ethernet cable will come with one in the packaging - it will work (usually). A good comparison is those cables are much like an old car - it should get you there, whereas this cable is like a high end sports car - it will get you there lightning fast, without failure.

This Cat8 is thin but still has adequate shielding within and additional insulation. The connector bases are reinforced at each end of the wire which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug. The connector plug itself is gold plated which is the ultimate standard in connectivity.

This Cat8 Ethernet Cable is 25’ long which makes it absolutely ideal for using it to directly plug your TV or gaming system into your router. So many of us stream programs and movies via our TV and there is no comparison in speed between a WiFi connection and a wired connection. For gamers, it is absolutely the way to go - do away with all lag caused by your WiFi by connecting directly to your router.

You will not find a better 25’ Ethernet Cable - this is really a top of the line cable that you’ll love.

This is an excellent purchase that you’ll never regret.

On my Lenovo desktop M700 PC, it came with the display settings for my Intel chip. When I right clicked the display, I would get an option for "graphics property" with Intel Logo. In advanced settings, I was given the option, similar to LED home flat panels to turn on Full Range, Limited and default mode. I set mine to Full range which instantly showed picture improve based off the image and much better color. So I set my PC to default color settings and turn on FULL RANGE mode in the Intel HD graphics control panel.

Some PC may have something similar not Intel based. I was also able to set the 1080p/60 fps on the monitor.

text_fidelity_a:
My Zone Wireless Headphones I got these headphones because I tend to put the TV on much louder than is comfortable for my husband, and the price was quite affordable. (That is to say, cheap.) Unfortunately, the saying, "You get what you pay for," applies in spades to my experience with this product.

I could not get the headphones hooked up by myself, and my husband, who is an IT guy, had to fiddle with them on and off over several days. He finally had to buy an [[ASIN:B000068O51 adapter]] to get it to work with our TiVo and TV combination, but while he could use the earphones once hooked up with little static, this was not the case for me. I had lots of static problems.

Here are the instructions we figured out to make it work with a TiVo, as well as it can be made to work once it is hooked up:

1. Pick up the headphones and the remotes for the TV and TiVo.
2. Stand directly in front of the TV.
3. Turn on the transmitter for the headphones.
4. Turn on the remote headphones by spinning the volume control dial on one side of the headphones. You might hear or feel a click when you spin the dial. A red light on the headphones will come on when they are turned on.
5. Press the Reset button on the headphones.
6. Put your finger on the Scan button on the remote headphones so you will know where it is.
7. Put the headphones on.
8. Press the Scan button.
9. You should now hear the sound of the TV through the headphones.
10. If you do not hear the TV, press Scan again until you hear the TV through the headphones.
11. You control the volume in the headphones with the volume dial on the side of the headphones.
12. You should turn the TV volume all the way down (or very low) using the TV remote since the TV remote does not control the volume of the headphones.

I rate this product as follows:

Ease of installation: 1 star
Ease of Use: 4 stars
Effectiveness of Product: 4 stars for IT husband, 2 stars for me, average 3 stars
Overall rating: 2.7 rounded to 3 stars
text_fidelity_b: My Zone Wireless Headphones

text_fidelity_a:
Led Ring Light 18 Inch Selfie Light Circle Light kit with Tripod Stand, Dimmable 3000K- 6500K Lights for iPhone with Phone Holder, Lighting for Video Recording, Makeup, Live Stream, YouTube Equipment Note: There is more than one product attached to this listing. I am specifically reviewing the 18” light.

One of the things I have been researching for a while is ring lights. I have wanted one for a little while, but not the kind that sits on a desk and is only useful for making personal videos for upload. I wanted one that would be suitable for taking portrait photos and would be suitable for professional use. This is a nice ring light to that end and so far I am pleased with it, though I have not been using it long.

This is a large light, 18” in diameter which makes it quite a bit larger than most ring lights available right now. It is large enough that you can shoot photos or video through it using a full-sized camera with little effort, which is what I was looking for. It comes with a full-sized tripod (which it needs) as well as a nylon carry bag. It also comes with a mounting makeup mirror in the bag which is something I will not use with the ring light (I have other uses for it). In includes all of the hardware you need for mounting your camera, video camera or phone if you are a vlogger or content maker.

The very first thing I did with this light was point my camera right at it while using the electronic shutter, in order to determine if the LEDs in this light are strobing or not. I half expected these to strobe based on the price, but they do not which is a very good thing. It means steady, consistent light that does not flicker.

There are two adjustment knobs that are on the light assembly, one to control the brightness and the other to control the light temperature. The temperature range (speaking in generalized, observable terms rather than technical terms with numbers) allows for setting the light from an orangy golden-hour glow to a piercing frosty blue, and everywhere in between. So, though it may require some messing it allows for getting the light temperature just right based on skin tone and background. The brightness can be varied from a soft glow to bright enough to hurt your eyes when looking right at the ring. Thought not designed for such, this would work as a studio light in a pinch...

I do not have a light meter to check the actual light temperature or the lumens/lux output.

There’s a plastic cover over the LED array that helps to diffuse the lights and make them easier to face when using the light to illuminate a face for portraits.

The power source is AC 110/120. Some ring lights I have seen and used have USB-based power input instead. These tend to be smaller and less powerful.

Construction is good though I would stop short of saying it is solid and rugged. It is mostly plastic so it does have some flex to it but seems sturdy enough to handle getting moved around and jostled some. Because the housing is plastic instead of metal this is a lightweight unit and is easy to transport. This is a trade-off I have seen with tripods as well – lightweight for travel, heavier for less mobile work. This light seems geared for the traveler based on that.

Overall, I am pleased with this light. It is a bit better than I expected and it has everything you need in the package to be suitable for vlogging or studio use. It’s a big light so it does cost a bit more than a lot of the smaller, USB-powered lights out there but the cost is reasonable. If you’re looking for a ring light that can be used for either video content or of portrait work, give this one some consideration.
text_fidelity_b: Led Ring Light 18 Inch Selfie Light Circle Light kit with Tripod Stand, Dimmable 3000K- 6500K Lights for iPhone with Phone Holder, Lighting for Video Recording, Makeup, Live Stream, YouTube Equipment

In addition, the cover of the case has little grooves at intervals so that the tablet can be propped up to be viewed at various angles.

As other reviewers have mentioned, it's a very sturdy and thick case, which does increase the weight of the featherlight Galaxy Tab somewhat. And as I have been careful not to drop it, I do not know how well it protects and from various heights...and nor am I likely to test! But it appears very solid, and the elastic cord sewn into the case cover keeps it closed well.

Drawbacks: there's no hole for the charger, so you must charge with the case open. Nor can you charge when using the tablet propped up. And you can only prop horizontally, not vertically, although I doubt if that is much of an issue for most of the things you would want to do with the tablet propped up.

In short, it's not perfect because of the case having to be open to charge, and I also wish there was some way to keep my stylus inside; the case is so tight that I have to hang it outside, exposing the tip to dirt and damage. But otherwise it works well for me. Your mileage may vary!

Dislikes.

I wish it was smaller. It’s much larger than I expected. Make sure you have enough room.

Overall.

I ordered the radio in order to listen to hours of Audible books at night. I usually fall asleep while listening, and it played throughout the night. That way, I wouldn’t be exhausting my IPhone battery constantly, as it uses a lot less battery life, when it doesn’t need to pump out volume. I have 2 Sonos systems and a bluetooth Bang and Olufsen sound bar. However, I wanted an easy to use radio right next to me in bed.

text_fidelity_a: GEEKOM Mini AIR11 Mini PC Windows 11, 8GB RAM Dual DDR4 256GB M.2 SSD, Mini NUC Computer with Intel 11th Gen N5095, Home/Business Mini Desktop Computer, 4K UHD/Dual WiFi/BT4.2/HDMI/Gigabit Ethernet It amazes me just how much power this little computer has.  It runs silently and generates almost no heat.  So far I have only used it with Wi-Fi and the performance has been quite good.  I want to try it with an ethernet cable, directly connected to see if performance is even better.  The biggest struggle that I had in dealing with this computer is that it has Windows 11 installed.  Not being familiar with 11, since all my other PCs have Win 10, I had a hard time finding some commonly used functions.  Of course that is not the fault of the computer.  There are some things to be aware of if you buy this.  First of all, you need a monitor, keyboard and mouse to use with the computer, since it doesn't come with these items.  Secondly, the computer seems to use all the latest connection types, such as HDMI for video.  All but one of my monitors don't have HDMI, but only DVI and/or VGA connectors.  If you don't have an HDMI connection on your monitor, you will need an adapter or adapter cable that converts the type of connector that you have to HDMI.  There is an included HDMI cable, with both ends HDMI.  There also is a mini display port connector, which I am not familiar with.  The mouse and keyboard could be another issue.  All my mice use the round PS/2 type connectors and some of my available keyboards are the same way with the old PS/2 connector.  To connect to the Geekom, you either need a USB keyboard and mouse (which will use up 2 of the 3 available USB ports) or your need a wireless keyboard and mouse.  Wireless may use one or two USB ports, depending on whether the receiver for the mouse and keyboard is integrated to handle both or if you have a keyboard and a mouse from different manufacturers, which requires two receivers, instead of one.  A good feature this computer has is a mounting bracket that allows you to mount it to the back of certain monitors, which is a space saver.  You really don't need this, as the computer is so small anyway that the footprint is minimal.  The only thing I would have liked on this is a DVI connector.  Also, the manual is very minimal.  Currently the computer goes to sleep after a few minutes and I have to press the power button to get it to wake up.  This could be normal behavior and I have an inquiry in to Geekom to find out.  I love this little computer and I will probably never buy a full sized computer again.  Storage is limited, but I keep all my data on external network drives and backed up to the cloud, so a lot of storage on the computer is not an issue these days.  If you can deal with the newer connection types with this computer, I think you will really love it.  I am really happy with it.  It is hard to find anything wrong with this computer.  I think it seems to be quite sturdy too, as the UPS delivery man just dropped the package with a big thump by my front door.  I was afraid it might damage the computer, but it worked fine, so I guess it can handle some bumps and thumps, as it was not packed with a lot of cushioning material.
text_fidelity_b: GEEKOM Mini AIR11 Mini PC Windows 11, 8GB RAM Dual DDR4 256GB M.2 SSD, Mini NUC Computer with Intel 11th Gen N5095, Home/Business Mini Desktop Computer, 4K UHD/Dual WiFi/BT4.2/HDMI/Gigabit Ethernet

A good comparison is those cables are much like an old car - it should get you there, whereas this cable is like a high end sports car - it will get you there lightning fast, without fail.

This Cat8 is designed to be thin, but don’t let that fool you into thinking that it lacks capacity - within the thin package contains the needed shielding and wires for super fast transfer speeds. The connector bases are reinforced at each end of the wire which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug. The connector plug itself is gold plated which is the ultimate standard in connectivity.

I used this 10’ cable to run from my router to my NAS - a primary connection where speed and a reliable relay is critical - and I’ve been nothing but impressed by this product.

You will not find a better Ethernet Cable - this is really a top of the line cable that you’ll love. This is a purchase that you’ll never regret.

text_fidelity_a:
Monoprice Blackbird 4K 3x1 HDMI 1.4 Switch - Compact, HDCP 2.2, Built-in Equalizer, 4K 30Hz, YCbCr 4:4:4, 18Gbps (Compatible with PS4/5 Xbox Apple TV Fire Stick Roku Blu-Ray Player) Since we mounted our TV we like to use as few chords as possible. This way they are neatly tucked along the wall and down into the entertainment center where all our entertainment equipment is housed. So the main HDMI cable runs down but of course we have more components that require a cable than the one connected to the TV. Our solution? A signal splitter. Thankfully, we have only three output connections so this one seemed perfect. Plus, it touts 4k signal, even though most pre-4k HDMI boxes should be fine, but it's nice to have that in the title just in case.

What I use this mostly for is the cable box and a couple of video game systems. As for the cable box, seems to work fine; no dropped signals that I've noticed, nor any degradation in quality. As for game consoles, I have the PS3 and the Wii U hooked up to it. SAme: no noticeable quality degradation nor input lag.
Now, to put it to the real test, I hooked up some retro consoles that have been modded to output native HDMI; that means they'll be HDMI with no lag. Considering I have this and two HDMI cables connecting the console to the TV, I was curious to see if there truly was any lag.
With older games, timing is everything, especially on the 8-bit consoles with platformers and fighters, like the NES. From what I could tell, there was absolutely no lag, not to mention signal loss. The buttons responded as though I were using a normal NES on a CRT.

So yeah, I'm pretty satisfied. It's a bit light and doesn't have heavy pads on the bottom to prevent it from sliding around. With so many cables, and the ability to use the remote control, it should be a bit more stable on the surface.
I haven't used the remote as the detections are instant. No need to manually switch the inputs, at least from my experience. Also, I didn't need to use the power adapter; the power from the HDMI cables seemed to be sufficient, and the detection was not complicated by the lack of adapter. Weird.
text_fidelity_b: Monoprice Blackbird 4K 3x1 HDMI 1.4 Switch - Compact, HDCP 2.2, Built-in Equalizer, 4K 30Hz, YCbCr 4:4:4, 18Gbps (Compatible with PS4/5 Xbox Apple TV Fire Stick Roku Blu-Ray Player)

Heysliy Product Photography Light Box 16x16 Inch,Adjustable Bright Photo Box with Lights,Portable Photo Studio Light Box Photoboxes are simple things; It is usually just 5-sided box with some sort of backdrop and a strip of LED. The Heysliy Light Box Photography lightbox is just that and nothing more. Designed to be portable, the box can be folded flat and comes with a carrying bag that nicely stores everything in the kit.

Unfortunately, it's the execution of the thing that is to be desired. The box is cut from a sheet of translucent plastic then folded to form a box. The flaps are joined by a barely-tight-enough screw cap that can be easily lost because it is not actually part of the box. The plastic itself is stuff, but has an elastic memory, which means that it wants to fold back to its storage position, weakening the sides of the box unless the flaps are folded outward first. Overall, the structure is quite flimsy and can be tricky to set up.

The Heysliy lightbox comes with four backdrops made of that paper-like material that is used by some reuseable grocery bags. The colors are black, white, green, and red. The backdrop is hung by a hole cut into the material and a tab that's cut into the plastic box. Any hard tug will rip that backdrop so be careful.

So the conclusion is that the box is annoying to set up and with the LED's mounted on the inside of the box, reflections will be a big issue with this box as can be seen in my pictures (nintendo switch pictured for size reference).
text_fidelity_b: Heysliy Product Photography Light Box 16x16 Inch,Adjustable Bright Photo Box with Lights,Portable Photo Studio Light Box

Still an incredible deal for this lens which came new in the standard Canon box with manual etc. (If it isn't warranteed - I can buy another and still be about the price of just one at regular price).

The lens itself: I was pleasantly surprised. I could have purchased it in my kit with the 70D camera, but wasn't really interested. For $140 - what the heck. The photos are sharper than from the kit 18-135mm STM IS lens in my opinion (and that's a pretty decent lens as kit lenses go). It is very small and light weight for a pretty long lens - especially on a crop sensor.
BONUS: Macro. It actually can get pretty decent magnification. Something like 1/4:1 from a pretty good distance at 250mm.
Plus it works great with extension tubes. I've used it with 12mm and 26mm (not together) and it worked great. Even autofocus - though I wouldn't recommend that for Macro.

Negatives (though - again - if you get it for cheap, these are quibbles):
- No lens hood provided. Buy a knock off on Amazon for $13
- Not a super bright lens. You're going to need some decent sunlight or a good flash with this. It ramps up to f/5 minimum pretty quick and f/5.6 not too long after that. Only the widest shots will get F/4.
- Pretty cheaply built (but it's a cheap lens!)

12x42 Binoculars for Adults - HD Low Light Night Vision - Compact Lightweight (1.05lb) - Powerful BAK4 Prism FMC Lens - Waterproof Binoculars for Bird Watching, Hunting, Sports -Phone Adapter Included In this $30-50 price range, I think you should stick with this one. We got another one listed at $40 and besides for the branding, it seems to be the same binocular with slight molding differences. The tech is the same. Don't bother spending a little more unless you really want to upgrade and get one with zoom function. All these economy versions do not have zoom. And if you're new to binoculars, there is a learning curve, but this is how you focus:

1. Set the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial to ZERO and set sight on a distant subject. I'm not sure what zero means since there are no numbers, but there are arrows, so I presume it's when the arrows line up.

2. Cover the RIGHT FRONT lens with your hand, and rotate the FOCUSING WHEEL (the middle wheel), until the image is sharp. Keep both eyes open while you make this adjustment.

3. Now cover the LEFT FRONT lens and rotate the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial until the image is sharp. So here, you're not touching the focusing wheel, you're adjusting the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial.
text_fidelity_b: 12x42 Binoculars for Adults - HD Low Light Night Vision - Compact Lightweight (1.05lb) - Powerful BAK4 Prism FMC Lens - Waterproof Binoculars for Bird Watching, Hunting, Sports -Phone Adapter Included

10.1" Car DVD Player with Free Wireless Headphone Support HDMI Input, Sync Screen, AV in & Out, Last Memory, USB SD - NAVISKAUTO If you are looking for a portable DVD player that has intuitive controls, a remote control and a case to hold the DVD player so you can view the screen while seated in the back of a vehicle, this is a good choice. The screen swivels around so you can fold this in half "backwards" so only the screen is showing. This is helpful when using the case for use in a vehicle.

Compared to my regular TV this is an enhanced viewing experience. I found this to be a better visual experience. All the colors were vivid and almost velvety. Whether I am watching a favorite movie or a nature DVD, the colors are fantastic. Greens and yellows are super crisp and water looks totally glossy. I can't emphasize enough how beautiful the colors are on the screen.

I found many uses for this DVD player. It literally became my entertainment companion for two days while I tried out every feature. What I loved best was playing my virtual fireplace DVD with a beach fire and ocean waves. The stereo sound on this is excellent, I felt I was really at the beach which made me happy.

The remote control works very well and allows you to do things like turn the subtitles on or off. The audio controls let you choose between various options. You can stop or pause the movie you are watching either from the controls on the DVD player or by using the remote control.

This DVD player also has a screen saver that comes up when you put it on pause or don't turn the screen off. There is a button that says TFT ON/OFF that turns the screen off when you only want to listen to the sound. I found this played CDs too so that made me very happy. You can listen with the stereo speakers or use headphones.

If you are looking to view widescreen movies, this works for that too.

This is perfect to take with you when traveling. The only caution is not to use it for yourself if you are driving. It does have a cigarette charger that will work in cars and RVs.

The only thing I do when taking out a CD or DVD is to turn the DVD player off completely.

Some other uses I found for this DVD player was to play relaxing DVDs before bed to calm the mind. I also watched an underwater DVD with fish swimming by. This DVD player allows you to have entertainment wherever you are. The battery lasts about 4-5 hours, but if it starts to run out you can just plug the unit in and continue watching.

The only thing I noticed that was different than a regular DVD player was when you are halfway through a movie, put it on pause instead of taking out the DVD. This does not seem to have any memory of where you left off so when you put the DVD back in it just starts from the beginning again. This is not a big issue if you just hit the pause button.

I'm very happy with this DVD player and it is fun to go into your own little movie world. This is handy to have when someone else is using the computer or main TV. You can watch movies anywhere you want. I use this mostly when sitting in bed.

~The Rebecca Review

I received one free DVD player for review purposes.
text_fidelity_b: 10.1" Car DVD Player with Free Wireless Headphone Support HDMI Input, Sync Screen, AV in & Out, Last Memory, USB SD - NAVISKAUTO

Jabra VOX Corded Stereo Headphones I confess, I'm not one for listening to things on earphones. I'm not attached to my iPod (I don't even have one). I don't listen to music on the bus or during lunch or anything like that. I have music on my smartphone, but I usually either plug it into the radio in my car via a cassette adapter and listen to it over the car speakers, or plug it into a speaker we got as a Christmas gift that is for use on music players/smartphones. So I all I had was a coupla dollar set of earphones from Micro Center when I absolutely had to use earphones. They were cheap and comfortable. Really, how much better can a high-priced couple of wires and earpieces be?

Mea culpa. I just did a head-for-head comparison of my cheap little blue earphones against these Jabra units. Wow. With my old earphones I could hear the fan and the television running in the background, and the sound was a bit smothered. When I changed to the Jabra VOX earphones I was awed. They were even more comfortable. The sound from the fan was completely inaudible and I could just, just tell that the television was on behind me, so I'm not saying they're noise canceling, but they do HELP reduce noise. The sound was excellent! The "smothered" sound was non-existent and the bass was especially good (I was listening to a podcast and the host has a nice deep voice). When I switched to music, the sound was much richer and I could hear a wider range of sound, and, again, the bass was excellent.

Plus the earphones come with a free app you can download that organizes your music. You can set playlists, view album covers, and it even has an equalizer.

If good sound is your goal while listening to your music device/smartphone, this is an excellent choice. My old blue earphones are going into the emergency bin as of now!
text_fidelity_b: Jabra VOX Corded Stereo Headphones

text_fidelity_a:
Eversame Bundle of 3Pcs/lot Multi-color 6 FEET 2M Fabric Braided Nylon Ruggedized Micro USB2.0 Data Cable Durable Universal Charging Cord For Samsung Galaxy S4 S3 S2 Note 1 2 4 Tab HTC ONE M8 X NOKIA Lumia PDA X-BOX Motorola, LG Optimus G3, PS4 and Most Android Tablets/Android Phones/Windows Phones (Black White Pink) Most of the USB cables I have are either 3' cables or are really short ones that come with electronic devices. Sometimes a longer cable is really handy, especially when the immediate area surrounding a work space is cramped. I looked to these 10' cables to help alleviate one such issue and I learned a few things. One of those things is that a cable can be too long in some cases, though this is a failure in organization, not in the cable.

These are flat USB cables. Flat cables are less likely to tangle than their round counterparts, but I will confess to preferring round cables anyway (it’s a personal preference, not a technical preference). These are shielded in woven nylon which is great; the nylon is stronger than soft plastic shielding and gives the cable a little more stiffness but does not make the cable so stiff that it’s awkward to run. The connectors are interesting - two-tone plastic that is different than anything else on my desk which makes it a lot easier to determine where both ends of the cable are plugged in. I tried stressing the cable ends at the connectors by trying to pull out the shielding from the plugs and they held firm.

I tried one of these with my phone and it worked just fine, I was able to charge the phone and move data between it and my laptop. I did not attempt a speed test.

There is a big difference between 3' cables, 6' cables and 10' cables. If you need a 6' cable, a 10' cable will leave you trying to figure out what to do with the extra 4' of cable. In my case this meant having to use a twist tie to bunch the cable up in the middle. This is not a criticism but rather a suggestion - get a cable that’s the right length for the job. If you need a 10' cable, these have worked great for me.

These are nice USB cables. They seem to be made well and they work as expected. If you need a really long cable, this is a good choice.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: Eversame Bundle of 3Pcs/lot Multi-color 6 FEET 2M Fabric Braided Nylon Ruggedized Micro USB2.0 Data Cable Durable Universal Charging Cord For Samsung Galaxy S4 S3 S2 Note 1 2 4 Tab HTC ONE M8 X NOKIA Lumia PDA X-BOX Motorola, LG Optimus G3, PS4 and Most Android Tablets/Android Phones/Windows Phones (Black White Pink)

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130) UPDATE: After over a year of using these, I have to say that the bad outweighs the good, especially for how expensive they are.

It is true. There is nothing easier to set up. But it's next to useless when you actually need it. They trigger way too slowly. And the batteries are not set up to charge or even work very well when it's really cold out, so even though they are close enough to an outlet for me to charge them without taking them down, I have to bring them inside to charge them when it is cold. But it's the slow trigger that really makes this system not worth the expense.

For example: New Year's Eve, someone wrote Happy New Year in the snow on my windshield. One of my Arlo cameras is pointed right at my car. I have a clip from before it happened. I have a clip from after it happened. If I did not also have wired cameras that record continuously, I would not know whom to thank (our sweet next door neighbors - they are so lovely!).

The cameras make decent deterrents. And they are handy to have when I need a live view of something. But if you want to catch somebody doing something, there are better options.

_____________
Original Review Follows
_____________

I'm going to give you the bad, then the just okay, and then the good. Short version of all that is that I wish these triggered a bit faster and weren't so expensive, but they are a substantial improvement over my older Arlo system. Skip to the end if you want to know how to set up the siren.

Bottom line: This system is not quite perfect, and it is quite expensive, but it is wireless, weatherproof, super easy to set up, and backwards compatible. I would recommend this to a family member or anyone else who needs a wireless outdoor install.

Okay, so the bad (and it isn't really that bad) is that the Arlo Pro cameras have some trigger lag. Depending on how fast the trigger is moving, you may catch them just as they leave the frame, or you might miss them altogether. If it's a person walking, no problem. A person walking briskly? Might be a little problem. Basically, these are better for a zombie apocalypse than for a werewolf invasion. I have a hardwired CCTV DVR system that is always "recording," so when it gets a motion alert, it "starts" the clip five seconds in the past.

The just okay part is that, for this kind of money, I wish the cameras had more configurability. I would like to be able to set the exact parameters of the field I want to monitor (currently, you can pan and zoom but that's not really what I am looking to do), and I would like to be able to set the sensitivity in a meaningful way (I live in a city on a fairly busy street and get hundreds of alerts/clips no matter how I try to minimize them). Additionally, the over-sensitivity is a drain on battery life, which is an indirect functional limitation on where I install the cameras. With batteries needing to be changed/charged within a matter of days, I need to be able to get to these easily.

Now for the good stuff:

I like Arlo a lot. I have three of the old ones, and even with the lag, they are great for outdoor applications. The Arlo Pro cameras are better. The video quality is better. While there is lag, it is not as bad as it is on the older models. These are also BY FAR the easiest cameras to set up and keep running. I have wifi range extenders throughout my weird old condo, and my Arlo cameras never drop their signals.

The Arlo Pro base station will work with your old Arlo cameras. I kept my old base station running, though, so that I can run different cameras on different schedules. It also works with IFTTT and with the Smart Things App.

The Siren was not intuitive to set up, but it is a cool feature. The default is OFF for all cameras, so don't worry about setting it off while you are setting your system up. You activate it in the settings of each camera - camera by camera. You can also trigger it from the smart phone app, so in the event that someone breaks in while you are home, you can turn on the alarm (better for a werewolf invasion than for the zombie apocalypse).

From the Arlo website:
To create a rule that includes a siren trigger:
Launch the Arlo app or log in to your Arlo account at arlo.netgear.com.
Tap or click Mode to access the mode tab.
Tap or click the Arlo Pro base station for which you would like to add a siren trigger.
Tap the pencil icon or click > next to the mode that you would like to edit.
Under Rules, tap the pencil icon or click Edit next to the device that you want to trigger the siren.
Select the Turn Siren ON check box.
Tap the pencil icon or click > next to Turn Siren ON.
Set the sliders for Siren Duration and Siren Loudness.
Tap < Edit Rule or click Back.
Tap Done or click Save.
Note: This rule is not active until you activate the mode to which you added the siren trigger.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130)

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Surface Book 13.5" (Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256 GB) So my only complaint about Microsoft devices as a whole is their lack of compatibility with Linux. This one is better than the other 4 I have owned. It still isn't working well with CentOS, but Kubuntu works awesomely, and I also have Kali running. I've got a tripple boot (with Windows as well) set up, and the whole thing took about 5 hours to set up. If you're looking for a laptop to run Linux on, that is light and has a great battery, the choice is this one or the XPS. The XPS (my friend has one) doesn't run touchscreen, but it is lighter than this one and gets even better battery...

Overall, this laptop has a great battery, a great screen, and runs Linux with very little effort. The only downsides are the requirement to have power connected in order to detach the screen (yes, the button does work in Linux), the fact that all ports (USB, SD and charging included) are on the base (so in tablet mode it can't charge, can't read an SD card, and can't use a USB device), and the fact that it is so sealed that you can't upgrade or repair it yourself. Those are the reasons I dropped one star (personally, I'd drop 4 stars for all that, but I know most people wouldn't).
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Surface Book 13.5" (Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256 GB)

StarTech.com StarTech.com 1-Port 10/100 Mbps Parallel Network Print Server - Fast Centronics Ethernet Printer Server Adapter - Windows 10 (PM1115P2) Customer service is 6 stars

I certainly would love this product if we could have gotten it to work. I'm on a 5GB wifi network, and the StarTech is for a 2.4GB network. It won't work with my Internet speed. Or so both my techie, Brian, and I thought. Keep reading.

However... I couldn't connect the print server (that's the little white box) with my laptop. I had a problem and got online to get it fixed. The chat tech was very polite, patient and knowledgeable, but pointed me to the support page that gave me step by step how to set up my wifi print server. Went there. Followed the steps but I had no idea what the server IP address was. Gave up until I could call and get someone to walk me through it. A survey came up asking for my thoughts on my experience. I told them I was having a problem and just needed to know what my server IP address was so I could set up to print from my laptop. Got an email from a supervisor asking if I'd like a more experienced tech to call me. Yes! I would.

Got a call from Brian. He was very helpful, patient, and walked me through everything. Then I had to let him have remote control over the process because it got too complicated for me. That's when we discovered that the print server wouldn't work with my internet speed. So I told him how grateful I was for his patience and help even though I couldn't use the thing that was going to save me so much time. We hung up and while I was typing up this 6-star review of StarTech's great tech support, Brian called me back and said he was pretty sure he'd figured it out. I gave him remote control again, and 15 minutes later I've got my wonderful wifi printer!! I'm so elated! It works.

I have Windows 10 OS on my Dell Inspiron laptop, and an HP J4540 printer -- 2008. They are now friends and talking to each other wirelessly.

I do not recommend anyone that does not know what they are doing to install this device themselves. I know a lot about computers, but I know when I need an expert. Brian is an expert! Installing the thing is complicated. If your wifi is 2.4GB, then you can follow the instructions on the website most likely without a problem. If you have a higher speed Internet, then there's a lot more backdoor stuff that needs doing. I have a feeling they'll be updating the instructions on the website for this kind of problem. But if you have any problems, contact StarTech tech support. They are the greatest this side of the sun... no joke!

WDX Grommet Hole in Desk USB 3.0 3 Port Hub BC 1.2 USB Charger with 3.5mm Audio Mic Phone Jack, 5V/2A Power Adapter for iPhone/Smart Phones(AC Power Supply Included) A couple of weeks ago I got a monitor stand to use on my desk. It had a large circular hole on the back of the monitor shelf along with a plastic cover for the hole. Apparently the idea was to give a discreet place to run the monitor's plug through. That seemed like a silly waste to me as you could just run the plug off the back of the stand with much less hassle. So the idea of this product, using that hole for a charger with some extra USB connections, seemed like a good idea to me. A real caveat though is that there are several essential details to pay attention to in using this item.

The first essential detail is to pay attention to the size of the hole you are going to use this on and the size of this product. Apparently those holes are not a standard size and some folks have had issues using this item because of that. Handyman types who have the tools to enlarge a grommet hole have an advantage here but it would behoove everyone to make sure this product will fit what they need.

The second detail to notice is that this device only works with USB 3.0 devices. The 2.0 ones won't work. My desktop computer has both 2.0 and 3.0 USB plugs. You can plug any device into any of those slots and it will work although the speed may vary. A 2.0 device plugged into a 3.0 slot will run but at 2.0 speeds. With this product, the 2.0 devices won't work at all.

The final detail to watch out for may be the most important one. Several people who have plugged the charger into their computer have reported difficulties it's created with their machines. So if you want to do that, pay very close attention the first time you try it to avoid any problems.
text_fidelity_b: WDX Grommet Hole in Desk USB 3.0 3 Port Hub BC 1.2 USB Charger with 3.5mm Audio Mic Phone Jack, 5V/2A Power Adapter for iPhone/Smart Phones(AC Power Supply Included)

text_fidelity_a:
APC Power Strip with USB Charging Ports, Surge Protector P8U2, 2630 Joules, Flat Plug, 8 Outlets More electronics in the home means a need for more outlets. An ordinary extension cord will do the trick, but if you want something that looks nicer, has more functionality, and protects against power surges than one good option is the APC P11U2 APC Surge Arrest.

This surge protection device is great for those who need extra outlets for plugging in electronics and other things. It has eleven sockets plus 2 USB ports for a total of 13 places to plug things in and keep them running. An indicator light will tell you if there is an overload, which is highly possible when there are so any plugs. We don’t have this problem because we use this on our kid’s tech table. It allows them to plug in their cell phones, tablets, kindles, and other items- all which use minimal power- and get everything charged all at once without them fighting over limited outlet availability.

Each of the outlets on this surge protector has a safety closure, which is good for keeping out unwanted items. This can be useful if you have young children- wouldn’t want junior sticking a paper clip or other item inside one of the sockets. And a light glows to indicate that the surge protection is working as it should.

If I could change one thing about this, it would be the length of the cord. It would be better if it was just a little longer because it would be capable of reaching further. But other than that, this surge protector has worked just fine for my needs. It has ample space to plug in and charge all of our household electronics, keeping them ready for use and protecting against power spikes in the process.
text_fidelity_b: APC Power Strip with USB Charging Ports, Surge Protector P8U2, 2630 Joules, Flat Plug, 8 Outlets

ZZN Bluetooth Running Headphones, Wireless Waterproof IPX7 Earbuds with Earhooks,Sport Earbuds in Ear,16H Playtime Sweatproof Headphones for Gym Running Workout, Comfortable Ear Hook PROS

1. Excellent sound for both treble and bass,
2. Well made, of durable construction.
3. Attractive appearance.
4. Water/sweat resistant.
5. Lithium, rechargeable battery, with a charge that lasts up to 16 hours.
6. Excellent range.
7. Built-in microphone, so you can use it to dictate with a voice recognition app or make phone calls. The sound quality for calls is excellent.
8. Comes with an attractive carrying case which is black with red trim .

CONS

1. The power button is odd. It seems to function somewhat differently than other Bluetooth headsets I have owned. Instead of connecting instantly, it takes around 6-8 seconds to connect.
2. The fit around the ears is a bit too tight for my own personal comfort. However, this is probably an inevitability, given the fact that earhooks have to fit firmly in order to not fall off during vigorous exercise.
3. There is no information offered on the country of origin of the manufacturer or, in fact, any information offered at all.

NEUTRAL

1. Be aware that, as is the case for all rechargeable, lithium batteries, the battery in this product will ultimately need to be discarded with hazardous waste.

HP Pavilion X360 14-Inch Convertible Laptop, Intel Core I5-8265U Processor, 8 GB RAM, 1 TB Hard Drive & 128 GB Solid-State Drive, Windows 10 Home (14-cd1042nr, Mineral Silver) It's not hyperbole for me to say I love this laptop. After working with glitchy, draggy old computers for the last year or so, this is a huge revelation for me. Not only is it fast on a task-to-task basis, but the startup and shutdown processes are incredibly fast. It's not wasting my time. Nor does it waste my time with a lot of bloatware. Yes there is some, but most is easy to remove should you not want it.

I like a smaller screen and keyboard, so this is perfect for me, and it's lightweight and has a slim profile, so it's easy to take along when I'm out and about. I love the way it converts to a tablet when you fold the screen back. Even the fingerprint recognition is dramatically better than anything I've had before. One thing I was skeptical about was the placement of the power button on the side. I was sure I'd be turning the laptop on or off accidentally, but I've discovered that it's not that simple, which is a load off my mind.

I could wish for a couple more USB ports particularly as I use both a wireless mouse and because there's no disk drive, so I have to attach an external one when I want to access files on disk. Eh, I'll survive it. There are always work-arounds.

Bottom line is that this laptop is a perfect match for me. I'm a writer (not a gamer) and this runs all the software I need, runs it fast and efficiently, and has tremendous storage capacity for all my files. I really couldn't have asked for more. Nicely done, HP.
text_fidelity_b: HP Pavilion X360 14-Inch Convertible Laptop, Intel Core I5-8265U Processor, 8 GB RAM, 1 TB Hard Drive & 128 GB Solid-State Drive, Windows 10 Home (14-cd1042nr, Mineral Silver)

SOLIOM S600 Outdoor Home Security Camera, Wireless WiFi Pan Tilt 360° View Spotlight Solar Battery Powered System, Motion Detection and Siren, Color Night Vision, 2-Way Talk, Remote Access,Metal case This is hooked to our wifi. In one picture, you can see how far it is from our house. It is about 250 ft from the house. There is a circle in red where it is hooked to a pine tree. This is about the furthest away we can get from the house while still picking up a continuous wifi signal on the camera. The camera really has a direct, unobsturcted line to our office window. Our wifi signal actually isn't super strong, so this in itself impresses me.

We have the camera pointed at our gate. Our gate is another 500 ft from the camera. We have no electricity at our gate or anywhere in between. We also have a solar motion sensor & doorbell that alerts us when someone is in our driveway, but this camera was our best option is seeing who was in our driveway.

I included pictures of what you would see were you standing under the camera and then actual pictures of what the camera sees. It is not perfection, but all things considered, for us, it is a step in the right direction.

App was easy to download. I do hate creating an account and then having to give up our wifi password and now I wonder who else on the other side of the world knows it? Oh well at this point. Set up wasn't exactly super easy, but I figured it out. Once set up though, it is near perfection. Solar panel has been outside and never once have I seen it below 100% charge and it is not getting full sun all day.

Overall, this met our expectations. I like it enough that I am considering another for our goat pen so I can keep an eye on mamas and babies. This would be perfect for that. No regrets here.

NeeGo Raspberry Pi 4 Screen Case for Raspberry Pi Monitor Touchscreen Display 7-inch I'm pretty happy with this case all in all. The only nitpicking thing I can complain about it lack of SD card access but that's just a once in awhile thing. I'll live.

Since there seems to be a few confused, this is a case. Nothing more. Reading the questions asked about this product makes me lose some faith in humanity. I'd love to live in a world where a screen and case cost this little. Oh, and yes you will most likely have to rotate the screen. Not difficult to do and not a flaw in the case. I mean, I guess you could say it's a flaw but how hard is it to type lcd_rotate=2 in a config file?

Buy the screen and mount the pi to it. Then 4 screws gets the pi mounted to the case. Without the back cover there's a decent amount of room for hats, although you may have to clip off the tabs for the cover. I had to do this to make room for an Ice Tower, not a big deal as I never intended to use the cover. This also leaves plenty of room for the camera cable to be routed should you need.

It stays put but for my application the mount angle is a little too shallow. Not a fault of the case as it's mounted only about 2 and a half feet from floor level.

Overall, not bad. I could have printed one but sometimes it's just easier to purchase something. Using for an Octoprint set up near my printer and it's been doing fine.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Voyage E-reader, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Adaptive Built-in Light, PagePress Sensors, Wi-Fi It's just plain spectacular how good the Kindle Voyage is.

I'm kind of a gadget junkie. Whenever a new Kindle reader comes out, I pass on the old one and buy the new. So I'm coming from a place that has used everything from the old Kindle Keyboard through to this, my newest Kindle, the Kindle Voyage 3G.

First, screen quality. I knew it had 300 v. 221 PPI I had on my PW2, but until I saw it, couldn't believe how much of a difference it made. Now, the PW2 screen is great, but this beats it soundly. For regular reading, I don't see any reason to switch from a PW2 to a Voyage, but I'd imagine that with illustrations and such, it would make a really big difference. I can actually read at one size smaller font than I could on the PW2.

The light: Nice light, no weird shadings. My device is smoothly lit from bottom to top.

Size/Weight: It's smaller, definitely (not the screen though). Couldn't really see any difference in weight between this and the PW2, but honestly, what's an ounce either way, especially once you start sticking covers on it? It's not something I particularly care about.

Storage/Memory: I wish it were a bit bigger. Not that I have any desire to have 2,000 on my Kindle at any given time, but once you get into using about half the memory, these devices always slow down and get ornery.

Wishes/Dreams for the next e-reader: That they'd include text to voice. I doubt this will happen, but I wish it would.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Voyage E-reader, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Adaptive Built-in Light, PagePress Sensors, Wi-Fi

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Chromebook 15 CB3-532-C4ZZ, Celeron N3060, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 32GB Storage, Google Chrome Electronics are a fact of life and most families have multiple electronic devices to get through their day. My family of four has four cell phones, about six different pcs, laptops, and tablets, and three printers. Now, we also have our first ever Chromebook thanks to this Amazon product.

Chromebooks, I quickly learned, differ from the usual windows or apple laptop in several important ways and chief among them is the limit on the number of things you can download. If you have specific games and other things you want to download, they may not work. I already knew this going in but I can tell from reading other reviews that some people were not aware that it worked this way and they now have a device with limited usefulness.

Once you accept the Acer Chromebook for what it is, you will find that it does serve as a handy device. It’s excellent for browsing the internet, creating google docs, using google apps, and pretty much doing all things google. I am already a google chrome user when I go online and I already use many apps from the google play, so what this Chromebook offers is compatible with my needs.

Looking at other specifics of this Acer Chromebook, it is about the same size as my old laptop, at least in terms of the screen size. The image is good, although I have seen other laptops/tablets with more pixels and sharper images. Still, it should be sufficient for most needs, and it has a good deal to offer for the price. I have noticed that the charge doesn’t hold as long as the manufacturer claims and the bottom of the Chromebook does feel hot a little sooner than with others. But the Acer Chromebook is still functional and it performs well enough for my needs.

Electronics are a fact of life and as much as we try to limit their use, they are here to stay. Since we have to have them and use them, it makes sense to get the electronics that best suit our needs for a fair price and this Acer Chromebook does exactly that. It does have its limits and it cannot do everything that a windows or apple laptop can do, but as long as you know the limitations before you purchase, you should be fine.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook 15 CB3-532-C4ZZ, Celeron N3060, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 32GB Storage, Google Chrome

iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey Last year I switched to a Macbook Pro 13-inch after being a PC user since the early eighties. I love my Mac, but I haven't gone whole-hog for the rest of the pricey iProducts Apple puts out. Still, this case is just about perfect for my needs.

First, I like how the zippered compartment for the computer does not unzip all around. It's really easy to slip my Mac in and out of its fleecy padded pocket while still feeling like it's protected. (There's also plenty of room for my little wireless mouse dongle, although I don't use a mouse much anymore.) The iPad compartment is similar, and it holds my Kindle Fire in its rooCase with room to spare for something else (like a checkbook or wallet perhaps). The clever half-case compartment with pockets for chargers, headphones, and pens has plenty of room for my Mac power supply, Kindle charger and cables, and another charger if I need it.

The full compartment in the middle of the case is for whatever you might stick in it. It's not huge in depth, but it would certainly hold a legal pad/portfolio and a magazine or two. I don't use a cell phone now, but one day I might, so the outer pocket for the phone is nice; it's also serviceable for one of those small flashlights or perhaps a set of keys (on the right keychain). Toothbrush! I could see using the sleeve as a lapdesk/laptop stand while seated on a plane or in a doctor's office.

The sleeve comes with a classy, comfortable shoulder strap with strong, reliable clips. At first it wasn't clear what the the clips were supposed to clip to, but they are hidden away under the edges of the center gusset (what you see as the narrow black line running across the thickness in the photo here). There's no tangling up with this shoulder strap, either; the business ends can be rotated to keep the strap straight.

It's lightweight. And the color? It's a perfect match for the Mac Lion startup screen, of course. Everything about it says "Mac," including the iHome logo, but you don't have to be an Apple nut to love this sleeve. Very well designed.
text_fidelity_b: iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Keyboard for Business (5KV-00001 ) I bought one of these 9 years ago and got a lot of use out of it. Yeah, the letters all wore off very quickly but I know where the keys are so no big deal. But it was finally time for a new one. The material on the palm rest was wearing out, etc.

I unpacked it and noticed it feels cheaper, oh well, not the first manufacture to make a product from cheaper materials as time goes on...

But the strangest thing... the little nubs you use to position your fingers are on the wrong keys??? On the left hand, it's under your index finger on the F key as expected. But on the right hand, it's under my middle finger on the K key. Makes no sense to have them be under different fingers. The middle finger, index finger I don't care but make it the same on both sides.

I already threw my old one out, and I could get it out of the trash but I tossed the dongle in the trash too would never be able to find it again...

The keys feel is Ok I'm not that fussy about key feel click, etc. but be warned that the communication on this keyboard with the dongle is terrible. It was bad on my original one and it's bad on this one. I was hoping there would be an improvement on that in the 9 years that I had the original.

In the end, unless there is something you really like about this keyboard (for me it was an ergo keyboard with no number pad) I would consider something else.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Sculpt Ergonomic Keyboard for Business (5KV-00001 )

We used this bracket to hang our new 75 inch Sony TV. The bracket itself has worked well. We did end up utilizing the extension bracket which gave us added mobility in locating the TV in the center of the wall. Due to our hanging the TV on an interior wall that had a narrow gap between the drywall and cinder block I had to get special wall anchors to support the weight of the TV.

Due to how this bracket is designed it can be difficult to access ports, such as HDMI and USB, once the TV is hung upon the wall. It can be done but someone must unlock it by pulling the straps and hold the bottom of the TV away from the wall as someone else navigates wires below. It is definitely not easily accomplished.

This is definitely a stable TV mount - even for large TVs, it’s just not the easiest to connect accessories once the TV is hung.

There is limited tilt mobility but enough to adjust for viewing angle.

This is a decent TV mount for large TVs but could be better.

I typically wear them for about 2-3 hours a day while working at my desk, and I have two major pros and three major cons I’ve noticed during the last month.

PROS:
🎵 The earbuds are super comfortable! I have multiple inner ear piercings in both ears (rook, daith, tragus) and a LOT of earbuds hurt after about thirty minutes. I can wear the Sudio N2s for several hours at a time. Small, medium, and large silicone tips are included so you can get a good fit depending on your ears. Sometimes I walk around my house and do chores with these in, they haven’t fallen out once.

🎵 For earbuds, the ANC is good! I can actually notice a difference with the ANC on and off; with some earbuds that claim to have noise cancelling, there’s really no difference. The ANC on the Sudio N2s blocks out when the television is playing in the next room, and even muffles the sound of the heater right under my desk.

CONS:
🎵 Battery life is not great. With ANC on, I get 4 hours, maaaaybe 4.5 if I’m lucky. I put the case on my charging pad every other day, it seems. The case supports wireless charging, which is a positive, or via USB-C. I’ve noticed the earbuds don’t always turn off when put in the case and the lid is closed, which undoubtedly contributes to the faster battery drain.

🎵 The earbuds support Multipoint connection, or connecting to multiple devices, but I can only get them to connect to my Mac. No matter what I try, they will not connect to my phone (Samsung Note 20 Ultra). I tried every suggestion in the online manual, but I can’t even get the earbuds to factory reset.

🎵 The touch controls are VERY sensitive. I have to make sure I don’t have any video tabs open when I put them in, or the video starts blasting in my ear. The only audible cue I noticed was to turn ANC on, and that is “Noise Cancelling.” A beep indicates turning it off, and beeps are used for all other cues. I don’t know what does what, I just wish I could turn them off.

Although the cons slightly outweigh the pros, I still use the Sudio N2s every day. The comfort is a huge factor for me. I’ve tried probably 8 pairs of earbuds in the last year, and this is the only pair I can wear for more than an hour at a time.
text_fidelity_b: Sudio N2 Pro True Wireless Bluetooth in-Ear Earbuds with ANC - Multipoint Connection, IPX4 Water Resistant, USB-C and Wireless Charging, Microphone, 30h Play Time with Charging Case (Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
Damero 2pcs/Set Portable Electronic Accessories Travel Organizer, Black I'll admit it right up front: I am an organizer junkie. I love having all of my things laid out perfectly and well organized in all of the different areas of my house. While I try to minimize as much as possible, if I do need to have a variety of items, and let's face it, electronics accessories and cords seem to multiply like rabbits, I want to keep them in an organized, attractive way so that I can always find what I'm looking for and so that they look nice on my shelves.

This two-piece set is meant to be a travel organizer kit for your electronics, but I'm using it in my office to keep all of the excess cords, cards, plugs, etc. for all of my various peripherals. It's fabulous, because I have one that I keep near my computer and one that I keep in my closet, depending on the frequency of use. If I need to get a cord out, it's right there, yet the cases are subtle enough that I don't feel like I'm looking at something overly functional all the time. It just looks neat, clean, and well-planned.

The quality on these is amazing. They are just stiff enough to hold their shape, yet flexible enough that if something's a little bit taller I can close the zipper over it and it's no big deal. The dividers attached by Velcro and so you can move them around so that it works perfectly around whatever it is you want to store and there. I've changed my mind a few times, and it takes two seconds to move the Velcro to hold everything perfectly in place so that it doesn't shift when you move the case around. I don't travel much, but if I did, I would definitely consider getting a second set for on the go. They are lightly padded and so would be a great way of keeping chargers, batteries, and other essential accessories safe. Honestly, I'm such a geek I would probably even use these for toiletries if traveling, because most toiletry cases seem like a messy jumble to me and I like how organized these are.

Overall, if you are on the fence about these, I would hesitate no longer. They are fabulous. I'm only bummed they don't make them big enough to house all the rest of the loose items around my office!
text_fidelity_b: Damero 2pcs/Set Portable Electronic Accessories Travel Organizer, Black

The remote has a quick access buttons for Amazon , Netflix and of all things IHeart Radio. They must have got a kick back from I Heart . The quick connect feature loose a plus for choosing I Heart. Hulu or the like would have been a better choice .

I would not be afraid to buy this set. I would strongly suggest that the purchase be supported by a vendor you trust and will support the sale after the fact. Bone Conduction Headphones with Noise Cancelling MIC for Clear Calls, IPX6 Waterproof Open-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset for Calling, Running, Bicycling, Hiking (Green) Bone conduction headphones have become quite popular and because of this, there are many to choose from. This specific model is quite minimalist. A thin metal frame with the vibration units and electronics hanging off it.

In terms of comfort, there is no adjustability to the metal frame so it may take some getting used to because the frame may feel like they are too big or too small depending on your head size. For me it felt a little bit loose but I came to realize that it actually stayed where you place it and it really wasn't a problem.

For sound quality, this bone conduction headphone will never match a nice pair of over-ear headphones but that really isn't what it's for. By leaving the ears open, one is still able to stay aware of the surroundings, making it great for cycling and jogging where hearing the traffic is essential for safety reasons.

A pair of earplugs are included with this product and with one or both in, one can really appreciate the difference between regular headphones and bone conduction. You can still hear the music (or in my case, audiobook) through the earplugs because of the bone vibration but all outside sound is cut off. This means that you'd be able to listen to music over the sound of a loud machine.

I have tried a few different pairs of bone conduction headphones and these are the ones that I have stuck with so far. The buttons maybe be somewhat limited (just two buttons that control volume and power), but they are easily reachable and not hard to press and the IPX6 means it's water resistant against rain and sweat.
text_fidelity_b: Bone Conduction Headphones with Noise Cancelling MIC for Clear Calls, IPX6 Waterproof Open-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset for Calling, Running, Bicycling, Hiking (Green)

HP Wireless Elite Keyboard v2 ...if you don't have a wrist rest or pad already, I highly recommend that you get one at the same time you get this keyboard. I was introduced to the chiclet- or scissor-style keyboard because of using one at work (using an Apple wired keyboard with an Intel Mac), and I have to say that I prefer it in every way to the more traditional keyboards. It is much quieter, and, for me, the feedback is pleasant. One thing I did not take into account, though, is that I had a wrist rest at work. So when I got this keyboard for home use and started using it, I loved it immediately--until the day I used it for hours on end. Then--ouch! My wrists began to ache.

Overall, this is a great keyboard. It connected to my computer without a problem, and the only lag in keystrokes I have experienced has been when the computer had just been "awakened" from sleep mode. For reasons I will not go into here, I am using this keyboard with a laptop: the laptop keyboard's lights indicate whether or not I have Caps Lock or Num Lock engaged on the wireless keyboard. I understand that won't help people using this keyboard with a desktop computer, but thought I'd put it out there anyway.
